text.p: TORONTO, July 30 Reuter) - The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE GLOBE AND MAIL: Canada plans fish offensive: Ottawa counterattack against U.S. would let B.C. fleet intercept salmon near border
-Sanctions to be imposed on Burma: Axworthy calls for tough Canadian stand against Rangoon human-rights abuses
-Greying of Canada oversold notion: Census says view 15 years too early
-Coveted FM spot awarded to CBC: No 'urban music' station for Toronto
-Hungarian diet proves deadly: Thanks to their lopsided taste for animal fat, salt and cigarettes, the country's middle-agedmen are dropping like flies.
Report on Business Section: Eaton's reduces store closings: Original plan was to shut 31 outlets; now monitor says 17 is 'probably the right number'
-AT&T unit sees profit next year: Boom in business long distance cited
-Torstar posts record profit in quarter: More than doubles year-ago results
-Molson aims to own 100 percent of its brewery: But unsure if Miller, Foster's will sell
-U.S. budget deal assailed: Leaders used hot economy to helphit targets, critics say
Big class-action suit slams Bre-X brokers: Lawsuit has particularly harsh words for Nesbitt Burns Inc. and its star mining analyst Egizio Bianchini
